name: Formlabs Inc.
subcategory: professional SLA/SLS 3D printers and materials (closed comparator)
origin_detail: Founded September 2011 in Somerville, Massachusetts by Maxim Lobovsky, Natan Linder and David Cranor, who met as students at the MIT Media Lab; launched the Form 1 desktop stereolithography printer with a record $2.95M Kickstarter in October 2012.
openness_notes: Closed designs, firmware and print-preparation software (PreForm) from the start. Openness is limited to interfaces: third-party resins via 'Open Mode' (Form 2) and 'Open Material Mode' (Form Studio 1), and a developer platform for customising materials and workflows announced with the Form 4L (Oct 2024). These are open interfaces, not published design files or open-source code, so the score stays 0.

license_history.note: No open-source releases found in the sources reached

risk_events: 2012-11: sued by 3D Systems over stereolithography patents used in the Form 1; settled and dismissed in 2014
2021: last disclosed priced round (SoftBank Vision Fund 2, $2B valuation); no newer valuation disclosed

2026-08: leadership reshuffle: co-founder Natan Linder left the board; CEO Maxim Lobovsky became chairman, Dávid Lakatos president; ex-Apple hardware chief Dan Riccio joined as advisor and investor and director Rob Willett increased his stake (amounts undisclosed)
2026-10: launched $699 Form Studio 1 (shipping from 2026-11-16), moving down-market into price competition with Asian resin printer makers
robustness: Diversified professional portfolio (SLA, SLS, materials, post-processing) with 'annual revenues surpassing $250 million' (company, Aug and Oct 2026), leading share of professional-class shipments (38% in 2025 per CONTEXT, via Wikipedia) and 55% of SLS printers sold worldwide in 2025; venture-backed with a 2021 $2B valuation, new insider investment in 2026 and no IPO announced; acquired Micronics (2024) to extend SLS. Customers depend on a single vendor for firmware and software.
physical_science_relevance: SLA/SLS printers are widely used for lab prototyping, microfluidics, dental and medical devices and custom labware; biocompatible resins (Form 4B/4BL) serve biomedical research.
openness_effect_assessment: Formlabs shows a closed, venture-funded hardware company from an academic lab reaching unicorn valuation ($2B, 2021) and about $250M revenue (2025) without open designs. Its main openness-related exposure was the reverse: incumbent 3D Systems' patent suit in 2012, which it settled. Its later 'open material' and developer-platform moves open interfaces to grow its ecosystem while keeping designs proprietary.
key_takeaway: Formlabs is the US closed comparator that scaled: an MIT Media Lab spin-out with about $249M in disclosed venture rounds, a $2B 2021 valuation, about $250M 2025 revenue and 750 staff, larger than every open desktop-printer maker in this group. It suggests that in professional additive manufacturing, proprietary integration of printer, materials and software captured more value than open designs did, with selective interface openness used as a growth tool.
